section: Home plate & infield at field level: backstop, dugout fronts, foul walls (night lighting)
title: At night the backstop, dugout fronts and foul-line walls are lit from behind and read near-black in the TV shots (extends H02)
seen_in: audit4/hp/n-tvc.png (crop audit4/hp/n-tvc-crop.png, side-by-side audit4/hp/cmp-backstop.jpg): http://127.0.0.1:5193/?hour=21 steps [{"file":"cam.js"},{"file":"audit3/seg.js"},{"js":"__start()","wait":1500},{"js":"__clean()"}, ...] then {"js":"__pitchAt(600,1.0); __app.cycleCamera('center')","wait":3500}. Also audit4/hp/r-tvc6.png (http://127.0.0.1:5193/?hour=21, __lastPitchBeforeSusp(1.0); __app.cycleCamera('center')), audit4/hp/n-dug3b.png (http://127.0.0.1:5193/?hour=21, __look(-6,1.7,-22,-24,0.5,0,55)), audit4/hp/k-backstop.png (http://127.0.0.1:5193/?hour=21&weather=off, __pitchAt(600,1.0); __look(-14,9,-6,6,0.8,13,28)).
reference: audit4/hp/ref/2987300364.jpg and audit4/hp/ref/2986440011.jpg (Flickr set 'WORLD SERIES', user heston, 2008 WS at CBP at night; https://live.staticflickr.com/3070/2987300364_3a23886a8e_b.jpg): under the lights the backstop brick is bright orange-red and the teal cushions read clearly as teal. hesb/2987306412.jpg: dugout roofs, fascias and field walls are all brightly lit. Sure: high.
problem: Behind the batter in the CF TV shot the brick renders about #24120d and the teal cap about #071412, both near black, while the grass in front is bright. That 12% band of the frame reads as a hole. There are three causes. (1) After dark the only strong light is the key directional light from the banks behind home plate (BallparkApp._stadiumKey = field (0.12,0.78,0.62)). It strikes every field-facing wall in foul territory from behind: N·L < 0 for the backstop, both dugout fascias and both foul walls. (2) The six tower spots (LocalLights 'stadium', intensity 2200, inverse square, range 380) give about 0.09 at 150 m, against the key's 0.75. (3) The night lift (s.emissive = col*0.35*night) is applied only in the field surface shader (Field.js fieldMaterial), never to walls, dugouts or seats.
target: In the 2008 night broadcast the backstop is one of the brightest, most saturated things in the frame: brick about #9c4a3c, lit to within about ±0.5 EV of the infield dirt; teal cushions #2a6e6a clearly teal; the navy dugout fascia readable with its white text; the first rows of the lower bowl lit like the field. Only the upper deck and the roof fall off.
fix: 1) BallparkApp.updateSun at night: scale the current key to 0.45 (it stands for the banks behind home). Add a second directional light for the outfield banks: field-frame direction normalize(0,0.55,-0.83), shining from the LF/RF towers and the 1B/3B roof banks toward home, at 0.35x the old key, colour (1.0,0.97,0.9). Give it no shadows, or a 1024² shadow map fitted to the pit. It lights the backstop face, the dugout fronts and both foul walls. 2) Raise the 'stadium' LocalLights intensity from 2200 to about 9000 (E ≈ 0.4 at 150 m). Aim the LF/RF towers at the backstop, e.g. field (0,1,5), instead of (0,0,-45), so the near walls fall inside the 34° inner cone. 3) Cheap fallback or complement: give the pit's vertical materials the same lift as the grass. That means Field._buildFence (wall-padding, backstop-brick, backstop-cap, wall-trim), Details2008 (dugout-roof-2008, dugout-band, wall-ad) and Field._buildDugout (dugout-rail, dugout-padding): add s.emissive = s.albedo * smoothstep(0.2,0.8,frame.night) * 0.3 * saturate(dot(N, toFieldCentre)). Acceptance test on n-tvc: brick luminance within 0.5 EV of the home-plate dirt, cushions visibly teal.

section: Infield skin (the dirt around the bases and behind the mound)
title: The infield skin is a smooth sand sheet that the CF telephoto resolves at about 7 mm per pixel: no drag arcs, cleat scuffs, base-path wear, granules or grass lip
seen_in: audit4/hp/d-tvc.png (http://127.0.0.1:5193/?hour=13&weather=off, [{"file":"cam.js"},{"file":"audit3/seg.js"},{"js":"__start()","wait":1500},{"js":"__clean()"}, ...], __pitchAt(600,1.0); __app.cycleCamera('center')); the bottom 19% of the frame is skin (crop audit4/hp/d-tvc-skin.png, side-by-side audit4/hp/cmp-skin.jpg). Also audit4/hp/n-tvc.png (http://127.0.0.1:5193/?hour=21, same steps) and audit4/hp/n-air.png (http://127.0.0.1:5193/?hour=21, __look(0,45,25,0,0,-22,50)).
reference: Scratchpad o_2987295982.jpg (3008x2000, heston 2008 WS; downsized audit4/hp/o_2987295982_s.jpg): the skin at 1B is mottled brick-orange clay with fine granules, footprints and slide marks round the bag, a darker packed strip along the base path, and a crisp, slightly ragged grass edge. img/ws_rush.jpg (Wikimedia Commons 'Players rushing field', Oct 29 2008): bright orange skin with a drag pattern. audit4/hp/ref/2986441627.jpg: the 2B/SS skin. Sure: high.
problem: Field.js fieldMaterial fills the skin with one colour (0.56,0.27,0.11) times three value noises (0.35, 2.7 and 19 per metre). The finest feature is about 5 cm. In the 5.2° CF shot the skin behind 2B sits about 95 m away, about 7 mm per pixel, so it reads as blurry, evenly lit sand. There are no drag-mat arcs, no footprints at SS, 2B, 1B or 3B, no worn trails between positions, no lip where the grass meets the skin, and no granular sparkle. Second base sits on a perfectly smooth plane. H04 covers only the 26 ft home circle.
target: CBP 2008 skin: brick-orange infield mix, dry albedo about sRGB #b8714c and wet about #6e3a26. Calcined-clay granules 2-4 mm, specked slightly lighter and darker. Shallow drag arcs round the mound and 2B (3-5 cm wavelength, 1-2 mm deep). Footprints and scuffs within 3 m of each fielder's spot and each base. The grass edge stands 2-4 cm proud of the skin. The base paths are worn darker.
fix: Field.js fieldMaterial, dirt branch: 1) Add a tiling 2k detail set (albedo, normal and height; 1.5 m tile). Sample it at p/1.5 plus a second, rotated sample at p/0.37 to break up tiling. Fade it by fwidth so it goes to the base colour beyond about 60 m. 2) Drag arcs in the shader: r = length(p - moundC); normal perturbation sin(r*2π/0.04) * 0.3 * noise(p*0.5), masked to the skin and faded near the bases. 3) Wear: a uniform array of wear centres (1B, 2B, 3B, SS, 2B fielder, the pitcher's landing, the base paths) makes those areas darker and rougher. Splat a footprint atlas (8 prints, 30 cm) by hash within 2.5 m of each. 4) Grass lip: in the grass branch, darken 15% within 8 cm of the skin edge (contact shadow) and lift the grass vertices 2 cm along the edge. 5) Keep the existing wet term (albedo x0.55, roughness 0.35) and the 2B puddles.

title: The backstop is brick with a flat teal stripe painted on its face: no separate cushions, seams or overhang, no camera wells at the corners, a net without cables
seen_in: audit4/hp/d-tvc.png (http://127.0.0.1:5193/?hour=13&weather=off, __pitchAt(600,1.0); __app.cycleCamera('center')); audit4/hp/d-backstop-close.png (http://127.0.0.1:5193/?hour=13&weather=off, __look(0,1.5,1.5,0,1.2,16,75)); audit4/hp/d-backstop-3b.png (http://127.0.0.1:5193/?hour=13&weather=off, __look(-12,2.5,11,12,0.5,9,70)); audit4/hp/k-backstop.png (http://127.0.0.1:5193/?hour=21&weather=off, __pitchAt(600,1.0); __look(-14,9,-6,6,0.8,13,28)); side-by-side audit4/hp/cmp-backstop.jpg.
reference: audit4/hp/ref/2987300364.jpg and audit4/hp/ref/2986440011.jpg (heston, 2008 WS; crop audit4/hp/ref-backstop-crop.jpg) show: 13-14 courses of red brick (about 0.95 m) under separate teal vinyl cushions about 0.30 m tall and about 2.3 m long, with rounded front edges and 2-3 cm gaps, overhanging the brick by about 4 cm; the brick meets the red track directly. At the 3B end, where the backstop meets the dugout, there is a sunken TV camera well with padded green rails, black mesh, a broadcast camera and a clear parabolic microphone dish. The Diamond Club's first row sits right behind the cushions. Thin net-support cables run diagonally up from the wall. Sure: high.
problem: Field._buildFence paints the top 0.3 m of the brick face teal in the shader (if v > 1.07: teal) and lays a flat teal cap on top. The wall reads as one continuous band with no depth, seams or overhang. The brick runs all the way to the dugout corners with no camera well. The net (Bowl._buildNetting) is a bare vertical plane.
target: Brick #9c4a3c with 1 cm light mortar #b8b0a4; the current 0.203 x 0.068 m course scale is right. Brick face 0.95 m, then a separate cushion 0.30 m high x 0.40 m deep, teal #2a6e6a (vinyl, roughness 0.45), in 2.3 m segments with 25 mm gaps, a 4 cm round-over and a 4 cm overhang. A camera well 2.5 m long at each end where the backstop meets the dugouts. 3-4 dark cables from the top of the net up to the suite-level facade.
fix: 1) Field._wall for the 'backstop-wall' run: brick face up to 0.95 m, and drop the shader's teal branch. Instance cushions along the run, n = round(len/2.3) per segment, each a bevelled box 0.40 x 0.30 x (L-0.025) (6-step round-over profile, material 'backstop-cushion', #2a6e6a, roughness 0.45), 4 cm proud of the face, restarting at each polyline joint. 2) Camera wells: cut the last 2.5 m of the angled segments FOUL_TERRITORY[5]→[6] and [8]→[7] into a 0.9 m-deep pit behind a 0.6 m padded front. Fit two padded green rails (Ø 8 cm, #1f4a3a, at 0.55 and 1.05 m), a black mesh panel, a TV camera prop and a 0.55 m clear parabolic dish (transparent, roughness 0.1); remove the seats behind (see HP07). 3) Bowl._buildNetting: add 3-4 cables (Ø 1.5 cm, #222) from the top of the net to the suite facade. On TV these are the only visible part of the net.

title: The mound is the same orange clay as the skin with a big soft dark blob; in 2008 it was paler buff clay with a flat table, two dug landing holes, a rosin bag and a crisp grass collar
seen_in: audit4/hp/d-mound.png (http://127.0.0.1:5193/?hour=13&weather=off, __look(-4,1.7,-13.5,0,0.2,-18.4,50)); audit4/hp/m-mound.png (http://127.0.0.1:5193/?hour=21&weather=off, __pitchAt(600,1.0); __look(-3,18,40,0,0,-18.4,8)); audit4/hp/d-tvc.png and n-tvc.png (the pitcher's feet at frame centre); side-by-side audit4/hp/cmp-mound.jpg.
reference: audit4/hp/ref/2986444841.jpg and audit4/hp/ref/2987300074.jpg (heston, 2008 WS Game 3; https://live.staticflickr.com/3039/2986444841_14a9bd09ba_b.jpg): the mound clay is visibly paler and yellower than the skin (sampled #d1947f vs #b5624c in the same frame; img/ws_rush.jpg, Oct 29: #fdca72 vs #eaa533). Dark packed clay appears only in the two landing holes 1.5-2 m in front of the rubber and at the rubber. A white rosin bag lies behind the rubber. The grass edge is sharp and the profile flat-topped. Sure: high on colour, medium on dimensions (taken from the rule book).
problem: moundHeight() is a smooth dome: flat only inside 0.3 R, then a smoothstep to the edge. The mound shares the skin's colour. The landing area is one soft 1.24 x 0.96 m ellipse darkened 60%, which reads as a stain. There is no rosin bag. At night the mound renders darker than the skin (#8a5b2e vs #a06b3c in n-air), the opposite of the photos.
target: 18 ft circle. A table 5 ft x 34 in (1.52 x 0.86 m), flat round the rubber at 10 in. From 6 in in front of the rubber, a planar 1 in/ft slope for 6 ft toward home, then easing into the field; the back and sides fall about twice as steeply. Mound clay about sRGB #c79a78 (about 1.2x the skin's brightness, G/R 0.75). Landing holes and the rubber pad #7a3f2c. Rosin bag 12 x 8 x 5 cm, #e8e4dc, about 0.5 m behind the rubber.
fix: 1) Field.js: replace moundHeight with a piecewise profile. h = MOUND_HEIGHT inside the table rectangle (|x| < 0.76, |z - zr| < 0.43). On the home side, a linear slope h - (d - 0.15)/12 for 1.83 m, then a smoothstep to 0 at R; the back and sides smoothstep over the remaining radius. Rebuild _buildMound with extra rings near the table. 2) fieldMaterial: moundK = 1 - smoothstep(R-0.05, R+0.02, length(p - moundC)); col = mix(col, vec3f(0.57,0.33,0.19)*scuff, moundK). Replace landK with two 0.35 m ellipses at x = ±0.25, 1.7 m in front of the rubber, colour #7a3f2c, with a 5 cm dip in the normal. 3) Field._buildBases: add the rosin bag (rounded box 0.12 x 0.05 x 0.08, white, roughness 0.9) at (0.35, h, -RUBBER_FRONT - 0.6). 4) Darken the grass 10% in a 10 cm ring just outside R (the trimmed collar).

section: Paint on the grass round home (the Phillies script and the World Series logos)
title: The 'Phillies' script is a Georgia-italic stand-in about 1.6x too wide, with stars floating above it; the World Series logos are about 1.4x too big and about 4 m too far toward the dugouts (extends H17)
seen_in: audit4/hp/d-tvh.png (http://127.0.0.1:5193/?hour=13&weather=off, __pitchAt(600,1.0); __app.cycleCamera('high')); crop audit4/hp/game_home_high.jpg, side-by-side audit4/hp/cmp-homepaint.jpg. Also audit4/hp/n-air.png (http://127.0.0.1:5193/?hour=21, __look(0,45,25,0,0,-22,50)); audit4/hp/d-tvc.png (the script is the red band behind the catcher); audit4/hp/k-backstop.png.
reference: hesb/2987306412.jpg and hesb/2986448333.jpg (heston, 2008 WS pregame, high behind home; crops audit4/hp/ref_home_high.jpg and audit4/hp/hs2_low.jpg). The script is the Phillies' own 1992-2018 wordmark: a heavy connected script with a looped P, blue stars dotting both i's, red with a thick white outline, about as wide as the 26 ft home circle. The WS logos are about 6.3 m across, centred about 12 m to either side of the plate and 4 m up the line (measured against the circle). hesb/2986447135.jpg shows the logo's colours up close. Sure: high on the wordmark, medium (±15%) on the measurements.
problem: Details2008._paintings sets 'Phillies' in italic 700 230px Georgia on an 11.5 x 3.6 m decal. Measured in d-tvh against the circle it is about 10.9 m wide, vs about 6.8 m in the photo, with thin serif letters and two stars floating above the word. The WS decals are 9.6 x 4.8 m at (±16.3,-2.8): their measured horizontal extent is 8.7 m (real 6.3 m) and their centres are 16.1 m from the plate (real about 11.9 m).
target: Script about 7.0 m wide, P about 2.3 m tall, strokes about 0.35 m; red #BA0C2F (it reads about #a8303c as paint) with a 0.12 m white outline; stars #284898 with a white edge as the i-dots; centred at z ≈ +8.5. WS logos about 6.3 m wide (quad 6.6 x 3.3 m) at (±12.0,-3.8), keeping the ±0.38 rad turn. Navy field #1a2f6b; white letters with a royal-blue #2a56b0 inline and a gold #c9a94a inner stroke; '2008' in gold on a navy pill; the MLB batter logo on top.
fix: 1) Trace the 2008 Phillies script into an SVG path and draw it with Path2D into the 1024x320 canvas in place of fillText. Put the stars at the two i positions inside the glyph box. Call decal(script, [0, 8.5], 7.2, 2.3, 0). 2) Change the WS decals to decal(wsMat, [∓12.0, -3.8], 6.6, 3.3, ±0.38). 3) Then apply H17's paint-into-grass shading (coverage mask, breakup by blades, wetness) to both.

seen_in: audit4/hp/k-dugout3b.png (http://127.0.0.1:5193/?hour=21&weather=off, __pitchAt(600,1.0); __look(5,10,-3,-23,0.4,-1,30); side-by-side audit4/hp/cmp-dugout3b.jpg). reference: hesb/2987306412.jpg (2008 WS). Crop audit4/hp/hs_lf.jpg: the 3B roof is lettered 'Citizens Bank Park' in the ballpark wordmark. Crop audit4/hp/hs_rf.jpg: the 1B roof reads PHILADELPHIA PHILLIES with an MLB logo at its RF end. audit2/ref/Home_Plate_at_Citizens_Bank_Park_(2372076348).jpg (Mar 2008): the 3B roof has green lettering, and the navy fascia repeats small white Citizens Bank Park logos plus 'New Era Fits'. hesb/2986447135.jpg: the 1B roof has red letters with a blue edge on white, and a thin red pinstripe along the field edge above the navy band. audit4/hp/ref/2986443709.jpg (crop audit4/hp/ondeck_ws.jpg): the 1B dugout has thick green padded rails with white 'phillies.com' pads about every 2 m and black mesh between the rails. audit4/hp/yt/OXKdNCcuEM8_hq3.jpg (Fox 2008 WS): Maddon at the fat, padded, green 3B rail. Sure: high on the 3B lettering and the rail padding.
problem: Details2008._dugoutRoofs puts the same 'PHILADELPHIA PHILLIES' texture on both roofs. The front rail in Field._buildDugout is two thin 5-6 cm metal bars, 0.55 m high and set 0.55 m back, with no padding, no mesh and no rail pads.
target: 3B roof: white #eeece6 lettered 'Citizens Bank Park' in the ballpark wordmark (dark green #1f5a3a), reading from the stands like the 1B roof. 1B roof: keep it, add an MLB logo (about 1.2 x 0.6 m) near each end and a 4 cm red #c8102e pinstripe 8 cm in from the field edge. Rails: a padded top rail Ø 9 cm, dark green #1f4a3a vinyl, about 0.6 m above the field; a lower rail at the lip; black 5 cm mesh between the posts; on the 1B side, white 0.35 x 0.08 m 'phillies.com' pads (red text) on the top rail every 2.4 m.
fix: 1) Details2008._dugoutRoofs: build a second canvas texture and pick by side (a[0] < 0 gets 'Citizens Bank Park' in '#1f5a3a'; use a serif placeholder until the wordmark is traced). Add the MLB-logo quads and the pinstripe on the 1B roof. 2) Field._buildDugout: top-rail beam width 0.09 in a vinyl material (roughness 0.6, not metallic). Add an alpha-tested mesh panel (the pen-chain-link shader with 5 cm square cells, #111) from the lip to the top rail, plus white pad quads with a 'phillies.com' canvas texture on the 1B side.

section: Field-level seats beside the dugouts (camera and photographers' wells)
title: There are no TV camera wells or photographers' wells at the dugout ends: the seats run straight down to the wall
seen_in: audit4/hp/d-dug1b-high.png (http://127.0.0.1:5193/?hour=13&weather=off, __look(-5,25,30,22,0,-2,40)); audit4/hp/k-dugout3b.png and audit4/hp/k-dugout.png (http://127.0.0.1:5193/?hour=21&weather=off, __pitchAt(600,1.0) then the __look calls in HP06); audit4/hp/d-tvh.png; audit4/hp/r-tube.png (http://127.0.0.1:5193/?hour=21, __look(20,10,-5,38,0.5,-16,40)).
reference: audit2/ref/Home_Plate_at_Citizens_Bank_Park_(2372076348).jpg (Mar 2008): at the LF end of the 3B dugout, a camera well with three TV cameramen behind green pipe rails, then a longer photographers' well. img/ws_rush.jpg (Commons, Oct 29 2008; crop audit4/hp/rush_wall.jpg): photographers in a green-railed well past the 3B dugout. hesb/2987306412.jpg (crops audit4/hp/hs_lf.jpg and audit4/hp/hs_rf.jpg): railed camera wells at the outfield end of both dugouts. audit4/hp/ref/2986440011.jpg: the camera and parabolic-mic well where the backstop meets the 3B dugout. Sure: high that they exist, medium on the sizes.
problem: Bowl._lowerTiers only skips 4 rows in front of each dugout (skipRows). Past the dugout ends (FOUL_TERRITORY ±(32.54,-10.56) to ±(43.54,-21.12)) the seats start right behind the low wall. The low-1B and low-3B broadcast positions, the photographers' wells and the cameramen that frame every TV shot of the dugouts are all missing.
target: Past each dugout's outfield end: a TV camera well about 4.5 m long x 2.4 m deep (floor -0.9 m) holding 2-3 broadcast cameras on pedestals, then a photographers' well about 6 m x 1.8 m with a single rail and stools. Both are fenced by the dark green pipe rail (#1f4a3a, top rail 1.05 m above the field) and step down to the level of the dugout roof. Also the backstop-corner wells from HP03.
fix: 1) Stands.js buildTier: add a cutouts: [{ seg, s0, s1, rows, floor }] option handled like inPortal (skip seats where S === seg, s is in [s0, s1] and r < rows). Emit a concrete pit box and a rail round it (reuse Field._pipeRail). 2) Bowl._lowerTiers: for the front segment after each dugout add { s0: 0.2, s1: 4.7, rows: 3, floor: -0.9 } (camera well) and { s0: 4.9, s1: 10.9, rows: 2, floor: -0.6 } (photographers). 3) Props: a camera is a 0.45 x 0.3 x 0.25 m body, a Ø 0.22 x 0.6 m lens and a pedestal, in dark grey. The operators come with the crowd.

section: Tarp tube on the field-level wall
title: The tarp tube lies on the wrong (1B) side as a plain green cylinder, too short for its 44 m tarp and missing its 'WORLD SERIES '08 ON FOX' banner
seen_in: audit4/hp/d-tube.png (http://127.0.0.1:5193/?hour=13&weather=off, __look(28,2,-24,40,0.5,-15,55)); audit4/hp/r-tube.png (http://127.0.0.1:5193/?hour=21, __look(20,10,-5,38,0.5,-16,40)); the right side of audit4/hp/d-tvh.png; side-by-side audit4/hp/cmp-tube.jpg.
reference: hesb/2987303394.jpg (heston 2987303394, 2008 WS): the tube sits in a loose green canvas cover with a long royal-blue banner, 'WORLD SERIES '08 ON FOX' (white serif, gold '08, MLB logos at both ends), along its field side, lying on the track against the low wall. img/ws_rush.jpg (Commons 'Players rushing field', Oct 29 2008; crop audit4/hp/rush_sign.jpg): the banner's MLB logo and 'WORL...' lie past the 3B (Rays) dugout's photo well, beyond two 'drugfree.org/playhealthy' panels. audit2/sheets/rails_tarp_2008.jpg (Mar 2008): the green-covered roll lies in the LF corner past the Toyota panels. Sure: about 75% on the 3B side; high on the banner.
problem: Details2008._tarp builds a Ø 1.3 m perfect cylinder (radius 0.65, roughness 0.4) along FOUL_TERRITORY[4]→[3] on the 1B side. It is about 25 m long, but the sheet it unrolls is 44 m. It is plain dark green with faint strap bands: no banner, no folds, round ends.
target: On the 3B/LF side, from about (-44,-21) toward the LF pole. About Ø 1.1 m, flattened where it rests on the track (0.95 m high, 1.25 m wide). Loose green canvas #2b4a38 (roughness 0.7; darker and glossier when wet) with slack folds and tie-downs every 3 m. On the field side, a 0.8 m banner: blue #1c3f8e to #2c64b8, 'WORLD SERIES' in white serif caps about 0.45 m tall, gold #e3b23c ''08', 'ON FOX' in white bold italic, MLB logos at both ends. The ends are bunched and tied.
fix: 1) Details2008._tarp: lay the roll along FOUL_TERRITORY[10]→[11] (the mirrored side), about 40 m long, bent at F[11] with two joined segments (a canvas roll gives). 2) Geometry: CylinderGeometry(0.55,0.55,L,32,40), with vertex displacement r += 0.04*noise(axis*0.8, angle*2), y scaled 0.85 to flatten the underside, and 0.6 m tapers at the ends. 3) Banner: a 4096x256 canvas UV-mapped onto the 110° arc facing the field. 4) Flip the sheet's pull in the vertex snippet (the u = 0 edge on the 3B side) so the tarp comes off the 3B roll at the suspension.

reference: audit4/hp/ref/2986443709.jpg (crop audit4/hp/ondeck_ws.jpg) and hesb/2987306412.jpg (crop audit4/hp/ondeck_ws2.jpg), 2008 WS: a white on-deck disc with the WS logo in pale red, on the red warning track about 2 m in front of the dugout rail, near its home-plate end. audit4/hp/hs2_low.jpg (from hesb/2986448333): each coaches' box is a single 20 ft line parallel to the foul line, and the 1B dirt path is wide enough to hold both the foul line and the runner's-lane line. audit4/hp/o_2987295982_s.jpg: both lines on the dirt at 1B. Sure: high.
problem: (1) In Details2008._paintings the onDeck canvas calls drawWorldSeriesLogo(), which starts with ctx.clearRect(0,0,w,h). Under the canvas transform that clears a 205x102 px rectangle through the white disc, so the alpha-tested decal shows a band of grass across its middle. (2) ON_DECK = [±11, 3.5] (game/Plays.js) is 5.3 m from the wall, on the grass. (3) fieldMaterial draws the coaches' boxes as full 20 x 10 ft rectangles (bpBox). (4) The 3 ft runner's-lane line at b = -3 ft lies on grass because the 1B path is only |b| < 2 ft wide.
target: A 1.52 m white disc (a mat: albedo 0.78, a little mud) carrying the WS logo, centred on the track about 2.2 m off the dugout face and about 2 m from the dugout's home-plate end: field ≈ (±13.9, 4.6). Coaches' boxes: only the outer 20 ft line, plus 1 ft end ticks. 1B path: dirt from b = -3.5 ft to b = +2 ft over the last 45 ft, so the lane line is on the dirt.
fix: 1) Give drawWorldSeriesLogo(ctx,w,h,{clear=true}={}) a flag and skip clearRect when the on-deck canvas calls it (or render the logo to its own canvas and drawImage it). 2) Plays.js: ON_DECK = { home: [13.9, 4.6], away: [-13.9, 4.6] }; the Director uses it too, so the on-deck batter moves with it. 3) fieldMaterial chalk: replace the two bpBox coaches' boxes with a bpBand along the outer edge (b = -25 ft on the 1B side, a from BASE-14 ft to BASE+6 ft; mirrored for 3B), plus 0.3 m end ticks. 4) Dirt: if (b > -3.5 ft && b < 2 ft && a > BASE-45 ft && a < BASE) { dirt = true; }.

section: Field-level walls down the foul lines
title: The field-level walls down the lines are plain dark-green padding with one Toyota panel near each pole; in the 2008 WS, navy MLB panels ('drugfree.org/playhealthy', World Series) stood just past the dugout wells
reference: img/ws_rush.jpg (Commons 'Players rushing field', Oct 29 2008; crops audit4/hp/rush_wall.jpg and audit4/hp/rush_sign.jpg): two navy padded panels reading 'drugfree.org/playhealthy', each with a small MLB logo, on the 3B-side wall past the photo well, then the WS banner. audit2/ref/Home_Plate_at_Citizens_Bank_Park_(2372076348).jpg and audit2/sheets/rails_tarp_2008.jpg (the 2008 regular-season set, Mar 2008): two red TOYOTA panels with the Toyota emblem on the 3B wall just past the camera wells. audit2/ref/Home_Plate_at_Citizens_Bank_Park_(2372062354).jpg (Mar 2008): a light-blue 'Independence Blue Cross / Choose Blue.' panel on the 1B-side wall. Sure: about 60% on the exact WS line-up; high that the WS wall carried navy MLB panels near the dugouts.
problem: Details2008._wallAds puts one 'TOYOTA Moving Forward' panel at 215-235 ft on each line. The rest of the foul wall (FOUL_TERRITORY 1→4 and 9→12) is bare dark-green padding, so the long runs down the lines in the high-home and follow shots are empty.
target: For the 2008 WS: just past each dugout's photo well, two navy #1c2452 padded panels about 4.5 x 0.9 m reading 'drugfree.org/playhealthy' in white bold lower-case sans, each with a small MLB logo. Navy 'WORLD SERIES 2008' logo panels toward the corners. Season signage further out if kept: red Toyota panels #c8102e with the emblem, and IBX 'Choose Blue.' in light blue #3f7fc4.
fix: In Details2008._wallAds: 1) Add adMaterial('drugfree.org/playhealthy', ..., '#1c2452', '#ffffff') panels with _fencePanel on FOUL_TERRITORY 3→2 and 10→11, just past the wells (t = 0.05-0.45, y = 0.15-1.1 m). 2) Add a navy WS-logo panel (reuse drawWorldSeriesLogo) on 2→1; on the 3B side the tarp tube (HP08) covers that stretch. 3) Move the Toyota pair to the next free stretch toward the poles.
